subject: botany
question_text: Give the scientific name of mango. Identify the generic name and specific epithet.

verification.note: Chapter 1 (The Living World) is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Botany Fastrack, book p.3 (VSAQ 9 of 9), which prints the question and a model answer but no star ranks and no year citations. Only one source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the board-paper back-test are both structurally impossible for this chapter; 'not checked' here means exactly that, never 'checked and clean'. page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Scientific name

lines.text: Scientific name of mango: Mangifera indica

steps.why: The binomial has exactly two words. In print it is set in italics; in a handwritten answer the two words are underlined separately.
common_mistakes: Writing 'Mangifera Indica' with a capital I. The specific epithet always starts with a small letter.
Underlining the two words with one continuous line. Underline each word separately.
steps.memory_tip: Mango and Mangifera share their first five letters — the genus carries the fruit's name inside it.
steps.margin_note: Underline Mangifera and indica separately — the convention is part of the mark.

steps.label: The two parts
steps.why: The first word of a binomial is always the genus and the second is the specific epithet. Strictly, indica alone is the specific epithet — the species name is the full two-word combination Mangifera indica.
common_mistakes: Calling indica the species. indica alone is the specific epithet; the species is Mangifera indica.
Writing the two parts in the wrong order. First word = genus, second word = specific epithet.
steps.memory_tip: Order rule: genus first, epithet second — capital word first, small word second.
steps.margin_note: Two labelled lines, one for each part, make the split easy to mark.

insider_note: The examiner checks the small-letter i in indica and the separate underlines — the writing conventions are worth as much as the name.
